analysis: Customers use Blinkit as a fast, mission-driven utility. They arrive with a specific item or basket in mind, complete the purchase quickly, and leave. Repeat buyers have formed habitual replenishment loops around staples such as groceries, snacks, and household essentials. Exploration is blocked by four forces: (1) trust deficits around product quality and returns, (2) price and delivery-charge sensitivity, (3) weak browse/discovery surfaces outside of search, and (4) satisfaction with familiar routines. Positive experiences are tied to speed and dependability, not discovery. As a result, Monthly Active Customers rarely try new categories unless prompted by urgent need, promotion, or an external trigger.
